title: Hybrid Computer Use: A Unified Programmatic, Semantic, and Visual Interface for General Agents
author: Haoqing Wang, Xiaoyi Zhang, Sicheng Fan, Zhexin Zhang et al.

summary: Computer-use agents increasingly tackle tasks ranging from everyday desktop activities to long-horizon professional workflows. Yet interfaces centered on screenshots and mouse-and-keyboard actions can impose a human-interaction prior, requiring repeated screen interpretation while leaving the computer's semantic and programmatic capabilities underexposed.
takeaways: We introduce Hybrid Computer Use (HCU), a unified interface for general agents that combines three complementary channels: programmatic interaction through code and command-line tools, semantic interaction through accessibility (AX), and visual interaction through graphical user interfaces (GUI).
A supplementary HCU skill guides agents in selecting and coordinating channels to use the unified interface effectively.
Our designed AX tools return compact observations, execute actions in batches, and report their effects as AX diffs, so the model needs fewer round trips.
